webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.hint: Each event is pushed to your endpoint as an OpenTelemetry log record, signed with HMAC-SHA256 so the receiver can prove it came from here.
webhooks.typesHint: Choose which events to send. With nothing selected the client receives all of them.
webhooks.rotated: Secret replaced. Update the receiver before the next event.
webhooks.examplesHint: Verify the signature before trusting the body. An endpoint that accepts any POST it receives is an endpoint anyone can feed.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.hint: Lets an external agent ask what the camera has seen, and ask the camera to start or stop. Nothing it can call changes the catalog, and no tool returns a stored image.
mcp.scopesHint: A token can do only what its scopes allow. Grant the narrowest set that works. camera:control lets an agent switch the camera on, so give it a token of its own rather than the one used for reading.
mcp.addressHint: Where the agent should reach this instance. The default is the address your browser is using, which is wrong when the agent runs elsewhere.
mcp.examplesHint: Configuration for the common clients. The token goes in the Authorization header.
mcp.toolEvents: recorded events, filtered by type, subject or time.
mcp.toolScene: what is in front of the camera right now.
mcp.toolSubjects: the people and objects this instance can recognise.
mcp.toolOtlp: the same events in OTLP form, for a collector.
mcp.toolStatus: which models are loaded and whether the hardware is accelerated.
mcp.toolCamera: whether a camera is wanted on and whether it is actually running.
mcp.toolCameraControl: ask a camera to start or stop. An open view honours it; nothing happens when none is open.
mcp.boundary: No tool changes the catalog, enrols or renames a person, deletes anything, or returns a stored image. The camera tools record a request; the camera itself is only ever opened by the view running in a browser.

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.hint: Lets a broker or a terminal subscribe to this instance as things happen, rather than waiting for an endpoint of yours to be called. The records are the ones a webhook delivers.
streaming.brokerOffHint: This deployment publishes to no broker. The HTTP endpoints below work without one, and turning a broker on is a restart rather than a switch on this page.
streaming.httpOnly: The HTTP endpoints carry the same records with no broker deployed: curl reads the events and any player reads the camera.
streaming.addressHint: Where the subscriber should reach this instance. The default is the address your browser is using, which is wrong when the subscriber runs elsewhere.
streaming.examplesHint: The shell needs nothing written. The browser examples use fetch with a reader, because EventSource cannot send the Authorization header these endpoints require.
streaming.scopeHint: Both endpoints read the credential from the Authorization header and nowhere else, so a token in a query string is refused and an img tag cannot be pointed at a camera. Watching one needs camera:view written on the token by name.
streaming.unavailable: Streaming is switched off on this deployment, so there is nothing to subscribe to.
